subject: Access controls for customer data — RBAC and support access (FinTrust)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Subject: Access controls for customer data — RBAC and support access (FinTrust)

Hi Jared / Maya,

Thanks again for taking the time today — great conversation. Quick recap and next steps from our side re: Access Controls / Data Handling: 

- What we heard: FinTrust needs role-based access controls with least-privilege defaults, strict separation between support/ops and engineering, auditable break-glass for emergency access, and clear logging/retention for access events. You also asked about how support access is granted for hosted customers vs Dedicated/Private options.

- How Redwood addresses this (high level):
  • RBAC: configurable roles (viewer, operator, admin) plus custom roles and resource-scoped permissions.
  • Least privilege: default-deny policies, permission templates, and ephemeral elevation for exceptions.
  • Support access / break-glass: time-limited, auditable "break-glass" sessions with mandatory justification and multi-party approval options. All sessions are logged and can be exported to SIEM.
  • Logging & retention: access audit logs are retained 90 days by default for Hosted; Dedicated/Private plans can extend retention and ship logs to your S3 or SIEM.
  • Data residency: model inference data is routed to region-specific pools; Private deployments support on-prem or VPC-only configurations.

Attachments: I’m including a short summary (redwood-access-controls-summary.pdf) and an example access matrix (access-matrix.csv) which maps Redwood roles to FinTrust personas.

Proposed next steps:
1) Please share your current access matrix (if handy) and any unique roles we should map.
2) Schedule a 45-min technical deep-dive next week with your security engineer to walk through break-glass flow and log export options.
3) We can provide a SOC 2 snapshot and more detailed retention options after the deep-dive.

Availability: I’m free Mon/Tue morning PST and Thu afternoon PST. Nikhil (cc’d) will join the technical call.

Thanks — looking forward to continuing.

Best,
Marissa Cole

Hi Jared — great questions. Short answers below, happy to deep-dive on the call: 

1) Break-glass workflow: By default Redwood supports a hybrid model: for non-emergency elevations we recommend a pre-approval flow (manager or token approver) before granting elevated access. For true emergencies, our break-glass allows immediate elevation but triggers a mandatory post-hoc review and multi-party notification (security owner + customer admin). We can configure your tenant to require pre-approval for the classes you flagged.

2) Audit logs & SIEM: Hosted includes 90-day audit log retention by default. However, we provide real-time log streaming to customer-managed S3, Splunk, or Datadog; once streaming is enabled you control retention on your side. For Dedicated/Private we can also mount longer-term storage as part of the contract.

3) Support access to inference data: Support engineers do not have unrestricted access to raw inference activity. Support sessions are role-limited to metadata and observability traces unless a specific escalation is approved by the customer (and recorded). We also support token-redaction options and can mask PII in traces for troubleshooting.

Attachments: SOC 2 snapshot (SOC2-snapshot.pdf) and the access matrix we discussed.

Proposed times for technical deep-dive: Tue 20 Jul 10:00–10:45 PST or Wed 21 Jul 09:00–09:45 PST. Please confirm and we’ll send a calendar invite with agenda & attendee list.

Thanks,
